REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MAY 9, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made during regular business hours by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and the document(s) will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, MAY 9, 2024, 7:00
P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos High School Boys Basketball Team.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce W. Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council honoring:

  Cerritos High School Boys Basketball Team (CIF Southern Section Division 4AA Champions).

  Jewish American Heritage Month (accepted by Alpert Jewish Community Center of Long Beach).

  Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month (accepted by Buddhist Tzu Chi Foundation,
  Cerritos Chinese American Seniors, Cerritos Folk Dancers, Cerritos Korean Soccer Club, Chinese
  Culture Association of Southern California, Filipino Seniors of Cerritos, Korean American O.B.
  Soccer Club, Mid-City Korean American Seniors, Rayshine Foundation, and The Original Happy
  Seniors of Cerritos).

 Mayor Solanki announced the meeting rules of decorum.

 Pursuant to City Council concurrence, the meeting agenda was reordered to consider Item No. 6,
 related to items not on the agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, to
 be considered after the conclusion of Item No. 11 during the meeting. Additionally, pursuant to
 City Council concurrence, a one-time waiver of City Council Protocol Manual Section 8.08 was
 granted and Item No. 6 was not televised or broadcast.

 CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed the Charter employees to schedule a report on the next agenda for
 City Council consideration to amend City Council Protocol Manual Section 8.09 – Order of Business.

 Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency
 members received full-text, unredacted copies of the seven (7) written comments submitted for
 meeting items by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record.
 Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during
 regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (Items not appearing on the agenda but within
  the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council)

  (Notation: Pursuant to previous City Council concurrence (considered after Item No. 5),
  Item No. 6 was considered after Item No. 11 during the meeting. Additionally, pursuant to
  City Council concurrence, a one-time waiver of City Council Protocol Manual Section 8.08
  was granted and Item No. 6 was not televised or broadcast. The details of Item No. 6 are
  listed below).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting agenda
  but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and Closed Session.

  Al Barlevy expressed opposition to the City Council’s participation in international politics.

  Teddy Lloyd requested the City explore the potential to acquire the tennis courts located at
  Don Knabe Community Regional Park, adjacent to the Cerritos Sports Complex.

  George Chalagonian expressed concern regarding Athens Services waste collection and
  recycling services.

  Michael Diaz requested the City Council adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Christy Mouk requested the City Council adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Maggie Fierro requested the City Council adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Juan Martinez requested the City Council adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Unidentified speaker requested the City Council adopt a resolution calling for a ceasefire in
  Palestine.

  Howard Sachs expressed concern regarding recent events at the Ivy Park at Cerritos
  assisted living facility and requested assistance from City staff.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Written comments, if submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda, are considered part
  of the meeting record and are available upon request in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer during regular business hours.

7.  Consent Calendar

  The Mayor opened the public comments period on Consent Calendar items. Seeing none,
  the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

7A.1. Monday, April 29, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  This item was pulled for separate consideration by Councilmember Johnson.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.1. (continued)

  Councilmember Barrows, Mayor Pro Tem Vo, and Mayor Solanki all confirmed that at the
  Monday, April 29, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting they
  affirmatively supported the consensus direction listed under 10B.1. on the minutes
  document, as presented.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Monday, April 29,
  2024, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Financial Reports

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated May 9, 2024 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  May 9, 2024  $2,091,913.80 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency dated
  May 9, 2024 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  May 9, 2024  $285,527.50 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.3. City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending March 31, 2024
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending March 31, 2024
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.3. (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as specified
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the Cerritos
  Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property with the C-4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for supply and delivery of compressed liquid chlorine, Bid No. 1545-
  24* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 2100 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under the
  proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of the
  CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report associated
  with this item;

  2. Award a one-year contract to JCI Jones Chemicals Inc. for an estimated annual cost of
  $60,000, with provisions for up to three (3) one-year extensions, for the supply and
  delivery of compressed liquid chlorine, Bid No. 1545-24; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Notify and direct commencement of the 2024 conflict of interest codes biennial review
  pursuant to requirements of the California Political Reform Act (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to notify and direct City
  staff to commence the 2024 biennial review of the City, Successor Agency, and Public
  Financing Authority conflict of interest codes (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7F.  Award of contract to RRM Design Group to assist the City in rezoning two sites identified
  in the City of Cerritos' State-certified 2021-2029 Housing Element pursuant to
  applicable State housing law* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 2100 et seq. (CEQA) that the proposed contract award is
  exempt from CEQA review pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines,
  based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report associated with this item;

  2. Award a professional services contract to RRM Design Group, in the amount of $61,250,
  for the rezoning of Sites A and 7 identified in the Housing Element, which are currently
  zoned Neighborhood Commercial (CN) and Industrial (M), respectively, and all
  associated actions required for such rezoning; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute any contracts, agreements, change
  orders, or amendments that may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Preliminary Combined Financial
  Program for the City of Cerritos and the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment
  Agency (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Shanelle Henry expressed support for Heritage Park facility improvements.

  Juan Martinez expressed concerns concerning City contributions to the Chamber of
  Commerce.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to adjust the 2024-25 Proposed City
  Council Travel and Meeting expenditure line item to $50,000 (total amount) for
  presentation to the City Council for review and consideration during the Fiscal Year 2024-
  25 City budget adoption public hearing.

  CONSENSUS (Council): Directed the City Manager to formally memorialize that the 2024-
  25 Proposed City Council Travel and Meeting expenditure line item of $50,000 (total
  amount) shall be divided up equally per City Councilmember ($10,000 each) and include
  this language for presentation to the City Council for review and consideration during the
  Fiscal Year 2024-25 City budget adoption public hearing.

  This item was received and filed and there was no further action taken.

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

10B.1. Review and consideration by the City Council of the City of Cerritos of Assembly Bill 2485
  (Carrillo), which proposes to reform portions of the Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  allocation process (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Assistant to the City Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to authorize the Mayor, on behalf
  of the City of Cerritos, to execute and provide a Letter of Support for Assembly Bill 2485,
  substantially in the form included within Exhibit 2 of the agenda report associated with this
  item. The letter is to be addressed to the California State Assembly Committee on
  Appropriations, with copies to be provided to author, Senator Janet Nguyen,
  Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva, League of California Cities, California Contract Cities
  Association, Southern California Association of Governments, Gateway Cities Council of
  Governments, Independent Cities Association and Gonsalves and Son (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, May 9, 2024, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B.1. (continued)

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  Robert A. Lopez, City Manager/Executive Director, provided an update on the opening of
  the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Each Councilmember’s comment period was limited to three (3) minutes pursuant to City

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Johnson, Yokoyama, Barrows, Mayor Pro Tem Vo,
  and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to schedule an agenda report for City
  Council consideration to commence actions to establish a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization
  to support operation and programming of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Request to approve or ratify City Council travel expenses for City-related business:
  Councilmember Johnson requested City Council consensus to approve her current
  and future travel expenses through the end of the current 2024-25 fiscal year
  ending June 30, 2024, as she had exceeded her $9,000 allocation, but not to
  exceed the total City Council allotted budget of $45,000 as a whole.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to process City-related
  business travel expenses for Councilmember Johnson’s attendance at the upcoming
  California Contract Cities Association 2024 Annual Municipal Seminar, as
  authorized.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to process past City-related
  business travel expenses for Councilmember Johnson in the amount of $876.75,
  which exceeded her $9,000 allocation, as ratified.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to process past City-related
  business travel expenses for Councilmember Johnson’s attendance at the recent
  2024 Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and
  General Assembly, as ratified.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Council Protocol Manual ad hoc working group
  to provide information for City Council consideration in the proposed manual update
